Civilization-layer record of the same: the Regent sitting of 2026-09-11T170735 (the 2026-09-12 Proofdelve docket) lost its launcher mid-sitting and closed out under session 2026-09-11T215229. CAUSE ESTABLISHED for the orphaned edict.begun of session 2026-09-11T170735, appended to the incident emitted at 21:56:52 which said only that the launcher 'died'. The Overseer reports the sitting was driven over SSH and the network connection was lost: this is a SIGHUP to the foreground process group when the pty went away, not an unexplained death and not a compromise. NOTHING WAS LOST — every commit landed 17:16:02-17:56:51, before the disconnect, and the sitting was idle-waiting on a human gate; no orphaned children, worktrees, locks or halt files survived. Two independent defects in bin/regent produce the missing announcement, and the second would defeat a naive fix for the first: (1) no HUP handling at all, where fort/scripts/fleet.sh:320 has carried 'trap "" HUP' since ForgeOs-dx34.3 on 2026-09-08 for this exact failure mode; (2) cleanup() stamps the handoff and echoes its WARNINGs to the terminal BEFORE the edict.ended loop, so on a dead pty an EIO write kills cleanup under set -e upstream of the announcement. Full analysis and the three-part remedy on fortkit-89f0, raised to P1; nothing applied, because bin/regent is this seat's own launcher and gate 1 exists for that recursion.
